demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
I think about why the event has happened to me

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
issues.explanation: The negative appraisal 'I am going crazy' fits panic/dissociation-focused PTSD presentations more than a guilt-based trauma of accidentally injuring another person. It is not impossible, but here it sits awkwardly with the rest of the profile, which is dominated by moral injury, self-blame, and prevention rumination rather than fear of internal loss of control.

Police as a trigger is questionable in this trauma context unless there was a legal/investigative aftermath. With the current profile, the other triggers and appraisals center on guilt, criticism, and moral failure, so 'police' introduces a distinct threat/authority theme that is not supported elsewhere.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Hypervigilance towards people: vigilant for dangerous people
issues.explanation: Being vigilant for dangerous people is poorly matched to the stated trauma type and the rest of the profile. Accidentally causing injury to another would more coherently link to self-blame, checking, avoidance, rumination, or sensitivity to criticism. Hypervigilance for dangerous people implies external interpersonal threat, but Threat is otherwise inactive and no other items indicate fear of attack or dangerous others.

issues.item: Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
issues.explanation: This item is not well supported by the rest of the profile. The trauma and appraisals are dominated by guilt, self-blame, and moral injury after accidentally causing serious injury, while there are no Threat items and the formulation specifically has inactive Threat links. Hypervigilant environmental scanning implies an ongoing external danger focus that is hard to reconcile with an otherwise self-blaming, meaning-loss profile centered on responsibility and prevention rumination. The other maladaptive strategies coherently fit the active Triggers ↔ Negative Appraisals ↔ Maladaptive Strategies loop; this item does not.
